metadata.title: HDBLAST: BD Prehistory Target Enclosures, Incoming-State Transfer and Finite-Band Ward Bookkeeping
metadata.description:

All23 files from published record23114217 are preserved; four additions give27 files totaling 448,387,915 bytes.

All36 rectangle pairs and72 component intervals intersect; maximum actual exported L1 radii are below1.555e-21 and3.138e-23, within the fixed1e-20 target gate. Fresh extraction replay in normal and optimized Python reproduces every DATA byte and scientific budget component. An independent saved-output review verifies the four runs and all proof/control receipts.

The exact prescribed source and zero-past condition determine the continuum target; no arbitrary state was substituted at the matching time. U and W are entire at k=0, while certified nonzero W(a,0) proves a simple infrared pole in A=W/(2ik) for both sources. The matching-time first-order Bogoliubov coefficients have opposite1/k poles and are not uniformly small at fixed represented epsilon as k approaches zero. metadata.title: Mutation by Natural Dominance: finite-sample bounds for recovery-corrected route comparisons
metadata.description:
Methods extension 0.5.0 adds finite-sample simultaneous confidence bounds for the recovery-corrected W/A/M route contrast in Mutation by Natural Dominance (TMD). It is a methods report with reproducible software and synthetic checks. It is distinct from archived software v2.6.5 and the earlier research-report version 0.1.0.

Main mathematical and computational result

The preceding 0.4.0 interior likelihood declined all-success and all-failure control tables. This update uses established Clopper-Pearson intervals and Bonferroni projection to retain observed boundary counts. For C prespecified contexts, twelve scalar intervals per context receive marginal two-sided error alpha/(12C). Projection onto the recovery-corrected finite log contrast gives an interval for each context. Rejecting a shared contrast only when their intersection is empty has false rejection probability at most alpha, conditional on valid marginal sampling laws, fixed prespecified analysis and route-relative control transport. Independence between components is unnecessary for the union bound; correct trial units and binomial/multinomial marginals remain essential.

Accepted numerical endpoints are conservative outer approximations certified with exact integer binomial tails. Exact rational bounds for J=exp(2theta) determine intersection; rounded logarithms do not decide rejection. The prototype admits at most 5,000 trials per scalar, 64 contexts and alpha from 1e-12 to below one. Observed zeros are retained; missing counts never become zeros. Structural true zero probabilities make the finite log target undefined. All-success controls can retain finite information; unbounded uncertainty is preserved. This is not a boundary maximum-likelihood fit, p-value, equivalence test, mechanism identification or externally novel statistical theorem.

Software review and synthetic evaluation

All 13 unit tests passed. Independent internal review checked the frozen source, endpoint certificates, exact binomial tails, rational-grid coverage, 4,096 projection corners and six deterministic fixtures. The repeated-sample diagnostic retains all 160 synthetic datasets: 40 exact reanalyses of earlier high-recovery stress counts and 120 new draws. The reused and new high-recovery shared-contrast scenarios each produced 0/40 rejections with finite compatible intervals; a deliberately strong departure produced 40/40 rejections; low-recovery stress produced 0/40 with unbounded compatible intervals. All true per-context J values were covered in these sampled checks. No dataset was replaced and no bootstrap was used. These are limited software diagnostics, not biological confirmation or certified power. Descriptive Wilson 95% intervals for rejection frequencies are 0-8.76% for 0/40 and 91.24-100% for 40/40.

In More Basic Terms

Recovering all 100 introduced control cells is useful evidence that recovery is high. It does not prove that recovery is perfect. We keep a range of possible rates and include uncertainty in the biological route counts. If corrected ranges across conditions have no value in common, that challenges the proposed common contrast under the stated assumptions. Overlap means the data have not settled the question. A control with no recovered units can leave a range unbounded; we leave that uncertainty visible. Exact arithmetic prevents rounding errors from deciding the comparison, but experimental records must still justify trial units, recovery transfer and independent outcomes within each binomial sample.

Scope, literature and provenance

A targeted primary-source review adds exact-binomial boundary-confidence work and recent whole-cell/DNA recovery and single-cell isolation studies. They inform measurement design; none supplies an authenticated matched TMD route-control panel. An archive audit also recovered a historical incorrect interval inversion. Original files remain preserved. No new laboratory experiment, matched biological validation, raw third-party dataset analysis, new physical law or external mathematical priority is claimed. Optional stopping, dependent culture descendants, misclassification, uncertain denominators and route-dependent transport failure require additional treatment.

Files and reuse

The new 0.5.0 PDF and reviewed ZIP contain the derivation, source audit, tests, count tables, seeds, exact rational targets, internal reviews, literature notes, checksums and In More Basic Terms explanation. The unchanged 0.2.0, 0.3.0 and 0.4.0 ZIPs preserve intervening methods releases in this research-report DOI family; they retain their own versions and notices. The earlier 0.1.0 report remains available as a preceding Zenodo version.

New report and documentation: CC BY 4.0. New software: MIT. Original publications and observations retain their attribution and rights. AI assistance was used in development, analysis and internal review. Neither EDISON grant 675419 nor MOSBRI grant 101004806 funded TMD. No research grant is claimed.

metadata.title: HDBLAST: Scalar Junction Consistency and a Corrected Static de Sitter Branch
metadata.description:
We examine scalar junction consistency in a specified five-dimensional Einstein-scalar shell model. The constant bulk field phi=1 solves the bulk scalar equation but fails the scalar boundary condition for the registered nonzero detuning. We construct nearby nonconstant scalar-profile candidates from a regular cone and impose both gravitational and scalar junction conditions.

At delta=0.001 and c=0.5975949350280132, the candidate has phi_b=0.9999159473169134 and H_b squared=5.9240147943293e-5 in model units. Six detunings, two producer tolerances, and 18 separate second-order Einstein integrations support numerical consistency. A regular Gegenbauer solution yields the leading scalar shift and the second-order expansion-rate correction. The registered expansion-rate correction is approximately -7.87 parts per million relative to the metric-only comparison.

The deposit includes a self-contained research manuscript and a computational supplement with source code, numerical profiles, exact identities, independent checks and reproduction instructions. It concerns reproducible floating-point static candidates and analytical consistency results. Stability, dynamical attraction, a global connection to the original configuration, interval-certified existence and a hot Big Bang mechanism are not established. No claim of external mathematical novelty is made.

This is a separate companion study referencing the earlier conditional linear-response record (10.5281/zenodo.22347452). It does not revise or extend that record's certificate to this nonlinear static problem. AI tools assisted with derivations, software, numerical checking and manuscript preparation; internal computational reviews are not external peer review.

metadata.title: Theory of Mutation by Natural Dominance (TMD) — v2.6.5: portable campaign execution and stricter result acceptance
metadata.description:
TMD (Theory of Mutation by Natural Dominance) v2.6.5 is an analysis-only software release for organizing and checking tests of mutation-route models. It builds on v2.6.4 (10.5281/zenodo.20186340), preserving the existing Zenodo version series.

What changed in v2.6.5

This update repairs Python 3.9 timestamp compatibility, aligns generated campaign manifests with the action and branch recorded in the replay ledger, and strengthens result-intake and submission checks. The tools reject the tested incomplete, malformed, or contradictory packages and handle malformed CSV files and reused output paths more safely. The source archive includes executable examples, regression checks, validation evidence, change patches, licensing, and SHA-256 manifests.

Validation performed

On CPython 3.9.6 and 3.12.14, on the same macOS ARM64 computer with third-party site packages disabled, each interpreter passed 2 acceptance gates, 4 smoke cases, 9 failure-injection controls, and 49 intake/integration checks. The 49 checks comprise 41 targeted regression cases and 8 checks using freshly generated runtime outputs across all four simulated campaign actions. The simulated campaign completed its expected four actions with the remaining budget progressing from 23 to 18 to 13 to 7 to 0. These counts describe selected software tests; they are not estimates of biological accuracy or general error rates.

Scope and interpretation

No new laboratory measurements or independently returned collaborator results are reported in this update. Validation uses bundled examples, simulated transitions, and intentionally invalid packages. It does not establish predictive performance on unseen biological data, an independent laboratory replication, or a unified theory of everything.

Replay and intake checks assess internal structure, consistency, and campaign bookkeeping. They do not authenticate a submitter, verify original experimental source bytes, or prove that an experiment occurred. Some legacy certificates and ledger fixtures represent separate simulated runs, and the legacy preflight certificate does not supply every input needed to recompute its root. The evidence and documentation state these limits explicitly.

Getting started

Extract the v2.6.5 software archive and follow README.md. From the extracted package root, run:
python3 -S verify_release.py
python3 -S runtime/run_tmd_release_acceptance_gate_v0_1.py --outdir runs/release_acceptance

The expected acceptance value is all_passed == true in the generated release-acceptance certificate. The README documents the intake/integration checks and next steps toward independent, preregistered evaluation.

Licensing

Software/code: MIT. Documentation/figures: CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise noted, following the May 14 release materials. See docs/LICENSING.md and file-specific notices. Earlier releases remain available through Zenodo's version history.

metadata.title: Quantized Horizon Response (HRF): Composite-Alternative Separation and Fixed-Conditioning GW250114 Replay - v5.3
metadata.description:
Methods and reproducibility release. Research package v72; Zenodo publication version v5.3.

This release makes available the corrected GW250114 HRF composite-alternative separation methods, numerical design calculations, and the archived fixed-conditioning -7M raw-grid replay, together with a September 2026 publication audit and reader guide. The original v72 archives, sealed on 17 August 2026, are preserved byte-for-byte.

In More Basic Terms

After two black holes merge, the resulting black hole settles down through gravitational waves, somewhat like a struck bell ringing down. This project investigates whether a proposed horizon-response model could eventually be tested with those signals. The archived calculation closely reproduces a reference grid when specified assumptions are held fixed, but changing the released parameter row shifts the best-fitting damping rate. Reproducing the calculation therefore does not, by itself, establish a new physical effect.

The statistical work explains why a finite measurement cannot uniformly distinguish one exact value from every arbitrarily close alternative under the stated continuity condition. A meaningful test needs a declared resolution, an interval procedure, or a specified Bayesian comparison. The progress is a more reproducible test and clearer limits on what can be concluded. It does not establish a unified theory of everything or a quantum structure at a black-hole horizon.

This is an independent exploratory research package, not an official LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA product.

Technical scope

  • Continuous-alternative closure: under the stated total-variation continuity assumption, the exact point target has zero uniform separation from the punctured continuous alternative; the stated randomized minimax maximum error is 1/2.
  • Least-favorable Gaussian design: one named competitor requires distance at least 3.7810604375 for target-side score exceedance of ln(10) with probability at least 0.90. The corrected symmetric two-endpoint rule requires at least 4.3486867653 per endpoint for a 90% joint-success lower bound. Effective-width screens at the historical gap are 0.115190902% and 0.100155239%, respectively. These are design calculations, not event measurements or automatic composite Bayes factors.
  • Archived fixed-conditioning replay: the 85 x 40 -7M grid has a released-row network maximum at 200 Hz and 450 inverse seconds, with centered cache-to-raw residual below 7.8e-5 log-likelihood units. Selecting another released posterior row moves the damping maximum to 420 inverse seconds. Active nuisance parameters change together.
  • The September audit verifies supplied artifacts and distinguishes fresh local checks from preserved raw-replay receipts. Official raw inputs are not bundled, and this publication preparation does not claim a new raw-strain replay.
  • A documented prose erratum corrects the recovery audit's signed residual label: the negative mean offset is cache minus raw, not raw minus cache. Centered residual bounds and gate dispositions are unaffected.

Limitations and next work

The full reference inference and its marginalizations are not reproduced. Detector-only remnant/QNM inference, global nuisance-image separation on a real joint likelihood, uncertainty propagation, and full-scan null calibration remain incomplete. Both detectors' event data have already been examined, so the accompanying proposed detector-disjoint reanalysis is a draft protocol, not a retrospective blind holdout or an executed study.

No HRF detection, exact ln(4) or g=4 identification, area quantization, black-hole microstate inference, or quantum-horizon discovery is claimed. The deposit preserves methodological progress without changing these physical interpretation limits.

Files and provenance

Begin with the reader guide and dated publication audit. The focused v72 ZIP contains methods, code, numerical surfaces, receipts, and manifests; the master ZIP preserves cumulative research history. SHA-256 sidecars and a publication file manifest support integrity checks. Historical reports retain their original July/August dates. September documentation and local checks were prepared with AI assistance in Codex and do not constitute independent peer review.

metadata.title: DMDE Triplepoint + CosmoGate: Five-Channel Weak-Rate Closure and Frozen-Pair Differential-Response Design (v0.9.20)
metadata.description:
Status: working hypothesis; methods/software checkpoint; not peer reviewed; no detection or production BBN-result claim.

DMDE v0.9.20 is a source-frozen validation and numerical-design release for a blinded two-card neutrino-spectrum to Big Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) test. It repairs a reproduced synthetic v0.9.19 false pass in which both charged-lepton capture channels were omitted and unblocked vacuum beta decay was returned at all temperatures. The new contract independently recomputes audit-only, neutron-lifetime-normalized Born histories for all five exported weak processes, applies per-process and direction-total envelopes, and checks the relevant threshold and endpoint refinement. It retains source-shape and time-integral closure, source-on/off production-stepper witnesses, and BBN input-consumption canaries. A companion source-only result derives the frozen pair's exact differential-response geometry and conditional numerical-precision requirements. The two physical source payloads and model parameters are unchanged relative to the byte-frozen v0.9.19 parent. The public packet contains the blinded provider files, validators, schemas, templates, documentation, and receipts. It contains no production helium, deuterium, or effective-neutrino-number result.

What changed

  • All five exported weak-process histories receive independent Born-envelope checks: neutrino capture, antineutrino capture, positron capture, electron capture, and neutron beta decay.
  • Each non-negligible process has a 25% audit envelope; each neutron-to-proton or proton-to-neutron direction total has a tighter 10% envelope. Finite-temperature beta blocking and the late neutron-lifetime gate remain explicit.
  • The momentum grid must meaningfully refine the antineutrino-capture threshold at 1.80433131 MeV and the beta-decay endpoint at 0.78233341 MeV.
  • Earlier source-shape, source-time, transport-stepper, meaningful-refinement, and BBN-consumption evidence requirements remain in force.
  • The source-only frozen-pair calculation gives an exact response identity and makes the numerical precision needed for future endpoint comparisons explicit.

Scientific status and limits

  • No production Y_p, D/H, or N_eff prediction is bundled or implied. No confirmation of DMDE or a unified theory follows from these checks.
  • The Born envelopes are execution checks, not a complete corrected weak-rate calculation. The frozen five-column export does not separately represent the inverse three-body process p + e- + antineutrino -> n.
  • Passing cannot prove that evidence was not fabricated or that transport, radiative, recoil, plasma, or nuclear-network physics is complete. Independent replay, physical review, and backend replication remain necessary.
  • The pair calculation determines a direction in source-amplitude space. It does not determine the sign or magnitude of any abundance response. Its neutrino coordinate includes linked source-energy and parent-density effects.

Files and verification

The original v0.9.20 provider archive is preserved byte for byte. The public README and release-note PDF explain the scope and next evidence required. The public verification receipt distinguishes software and archive checks from missing production results. The SHA-256 manifest covers the public files. Private analyst scoring and unblinding material is excluded.

Source release: 17 August 2026. Explanatory note prepared: 5 September 2026. This is a methods/software checkpoint with production execution and independent replication still pending.

metadata.title: Unified Theory of Everything Research Program: TOE-N00AK-r1 - Exact Tree-Level Majorana Kernels and a Dimension-Seven Scope Correction
metadata.description:
This research and reproducibility update documents the sequential Type-I seesaw effective-field-theory branch of the project. It retains exact tree-level identities and corrects the interpretation of the earlier local TOE-N00AK dimension-seven loop claims.

Established mathematical content: the lepton-number-violating finite-pole Majorana tree kernel, its local moments and exact remainder, a spectral-norm error bound, and finite-pole reconstruction from the first c effective-node moments when those nodes are known. For a single nonzero removed pole at a probe-to-heavy mass ratio r below one, retaining dimension five gives relative tree-kernel error r^2; retaining dimensions five and seven gives r^4. These are tree-kernel approximation errors, not uncertainties on measured neutrino masses.

Scope correction: the proposed dimension-seven bubble was obtained by multiplying a published dimension-five result by a common external momentum squared. The derivative LLHH vertex has distinct Wick pairings with different composite momenta; one pairing carries loop momentum. The supplied argument therefore does not establish the dimension-seven ultraviolet pole. The proposed +3 A2 and -3 A2 components, their higher-odd extensions, and their finite-ratio cancellation are retained only as conditional algebra, not established loop coefficients. A common coefficient other than 3 also cancels, demonstrating why algebraic replay cannot determine that physical coefficient. This identifies a gap in the derivation; it does not calculate a replacement coefficient or prove the eventual physical cancellation false.

The release contains a corrected technical note, a readable PDF overview, frozen benchmark data, a focused numerical implementation, fresh verification results, and file checksums. Code checks establish reproducibility of the stated mathematical and conditional formulas. AI-assisted checks are not independent expert peer review. Historical parent archives and private chat exports are excluded.

The next calculation is an independently routed off-shell dimension-seven mixed-bubble evaluation with all Wick contractions and complete sourced-equation-of-motion reduction. The full dimension-seven operator packet, hard and finite one-loop matching, and connection to low-energy observables remain open. This release does not demonstrate a complete Theory of Everything, a new experimentally validated prediction, or a physical bridge joining the earlier epsilon-lattice construction to a complete ultraviolet theory.

What this record contains. A reproducibility‑first bundle for HDBC v3.9: (i) publication‑style overlays and SNR maps using the collaboration‑grade PISC/PLI kernels and noise PSDs for LISA/DECIGO (via path‑driven CSV loaders), (ii) a geometry‑exact DECIGO two‑cluster overlap function γ_KT(f), (iii) sub‑mm gravity α–λ CSVs (Eöt‑Wash/HUST) to re‑shade the exclusion band, (iv) a ΔN_eff(a) track for light‑weight BBN/CMB emulation, and (v) a camera‑ready PDF with the triangle relation, posterior panel, and no‑go bound.

How to switch to official kernels. Place the collaboration archives (PSDs, PLI, PISC) in `/data/pisc_pli/` and extract in place; the loaders auto‑detect these paths. CSV header format is `frequency_Hz,Omega_floor`. See `HDBC_official_readme.txt` and the manifest for canonical paths.

License. Dataset © 2025, CC‑BY‑4.0. Third‑party kernel tables are CC‑BY‑4.0 from the collaboration’s Zenodo and credited in the README.

How to switch to official kernels
---------------------------------
Drop the collaboration CSVs with header:
    frequency_Hz,Omega_floor
into your working directory and use the tiny loader included here:

from HDBC_official_response_hooks import get_lisa_floor, get_decigo_floor
lisa_floor   = get_lisa_floor("lisa_official_Omega_floor.csv")
decigo_floor = get_decigo_floor("decigo_official_Omega_floor.csv")

The figures regenerate automatically once the floors are present; the
gray ξ_sw ∈ [0.3, 1] systematics prior box and labels are unchanged.
references: Caprini, C., et al. "Detecting gravitational waves from cosmological phase transitions." JCAP (review). Schmitz, K. "New approaches to stochastic gravitational‑wave backgrounds." (PISC/PLI methods). Eöt‑Wash and HUST torsion‑balance bounds on sub‑mm gravity (α–λ summary papers). Planck Collaboration (2018); ACT DR6: constraints on N_eff and damping tail. Cremades, Ibáñez, Marchesano (2004): Yukawas from intersecting branes (Jacobi‑θ overlaps). Green–Schwarz (1984): anomaly cancellation mechanism.
metadata.notes:
Higher‑Dimensional Blast Cosmology (HDBC): kernels‑accurate GW overlays, sub‑mm constraints, and BBN posteriors.

We release HDBC v3.9, a reproducibility‑first bundle coupling a higher‑dimensional “blast” microphysics ansatz to observational pipelines spanning space‑borne GW interferometers and early‑universe probes. Using the official peak/power‑law integrated sensitivity kernels and noise PSDs, we produce publication‑accurate SNR/PLI/PISC overlays for LISA and DECIGO/B‑DECIGO. A geometry‑exact DECIGO two‑cluster overlap function γ_KT(f) is supplied for D=1200 km, 60° arms, 15° tilt. On sub‑millimeter scales, we provide publication‑exact Eöt‑Wash/HUST α–λ CSVs to shade the exclusion band. A ΔN_eff(a) track enables light‑weight BBN/CMB emulation of Y_p and D/H posteriors. Appendices tabulate D‑brane GS couplings (massless Y), intersections, and Yukawa matrices. All artifacts are path‑driven, documented, and accompanied by a manifest, enabling exact reproduction without code edits.

Manifest & README. Paths under `/data/pisc_pli/`, `/data/submm_bounds/`, and the track at `/DeltaNeff_track.csv`. That ensures others can reproduce your figures without editing code paths.

Official kernels. The `fetch_pisc_pli.sh` + README tell users how to pull the official Schmitz PISC/PLI/PSD tables and extract them in place—perfect for reproducibility.

title: Higher‑Dimensional Blast Cosmology (HDBC) v3.9 — Reproducibility bundle: official PISC/PLI overlays, DECIGO γ(f), sub‑mm α→λ bounds, and BBN/CMB posteriors.

metadata.title: Data & Repro Pack (REALDATA; v1.2.1): a brane‑world two‑link test (λ → {f_br, ΔN_eff})
metadata.description:
Zenodo v1.2.1 — Data & Repro Pack (REALDATA; evidence panel + λ–ΔN_eff scatter + LISA strip)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This pack contains all core, reproducible artifacts for
“The Maldonado two‑link test (λ → {f_br, ΔN_eff})” — a single early‑universe parameter controlling
(i) the break frequency f_br in the SGWB and (ii) a small early‑radiation excess ΔN_eff.

Key invariants:
  • f_br(λ) ∝ λ^(1/4)
  • C/ρ_γ0 = (7/8)*(4/11)^(4/3)*ΔN_eff

What’s new in this v1.2.1 drop
  • Evidence panel: ΔAIC/ΔBIC bars + a clearly labeled BIC→Bayes approximation panel.
  • LISA forecast strip: a vertical band at f_br (median ± 1σ) over a wide frequency axis.
  • λ_phys – ΔN_eff scatter (single-plot quick-look) in Corner_LambdaPhys_DNeff_20250817.pdf.
  • Harmonized BestFit JSON with calibrated f_br ↔ T_x ↔ λ_phys mapping.

Files in this pack (core selection):
  • PRD_Letter_FINAL_20250819.pdf
  • TwoPager_FINAL_20250819.pdf
  • Handout_PRD_OnePage_FINAL_20250819.pdf
  • Handout_TwoPager_OnePage_FINAL_20250819.pdf
  • Slide_Maldonado_TwoLink_Summary_20250819.pdf
  • Evidence_Summary_20250819.csv, Evidence_Summary_20250819.txt
  • Evidence_BarChart_20250819.png
  • BBN_Safety_Speedup_20250819.png
  • PTA_Overlay_fbr_20250819.png  (and/or PTA_Overlay_CORRECTED_20250819.png if present)
  • LISA_Overlay_fbr_20250819.png (and/or LISA_Overlay_CORRECTED_20250819.png if present)
  • LISA_ForecastStrip_20250817.png
  • Corner_LambdaPhys_DNeff_20250817.pdf
  • BestFit_JOINT_REALDATA_20250819.json
  • TwoLink_Summary_20250819.md
  • Holographic_Dictionary_Maldonado_Link_20250819.md
  • Criteria_Checklist_Update_20250819.md
  • maldonado_two_link_repro_v1.py

Reproduction
  1) Read f_br, λ_phys, and ΔN_eff from BestFit_JOINT_REALDATA_20250819.json to regenerate the summary figures.
  2) Use maldonado_two_link_repro_v1.py to rebuild the Evidence panels and overlays from the CSV/TXT in this pack.
  3) For PTA/LISA context, overlay your preferred sensitivity curves (if you have ESA-style CSV), or use the provided quick-look PNGs.

Licensing

  • Code: MIT or Apache 2.0 recommended (license header included inside the script if you choose).

Citation
